'''Kenneth J. Dunkley''' (born 1939) is an American [[physicist]], [[inventor]] and business man. He is best known in the field of [[holography]] for inventing and patenting [[3-D glasses|Three Dimensional Viewing Glasses]] (3-DVG).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Black History, Kenneth J. Dunkley|url=https://www.famu.edu/index.cfm?blackhistory&KennethJ.Dunkley|url-status=dead|access-date=2021-02-04|website=Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University|archive-date=2021-02-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206041936/https://www.famu.edu/index.cfm?blackhistory&KennethJ.Dunkley}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2019-10-04|title=If you were able to watch Avatar in a theatre with 3D glasses, all the credit goes to this man|url=https://face2faceafrica.com/article/if-you-were-able-to-watch-avatar-in-a-theatre-with-3d-glasses-all-the-credit-goes-to-this-man|access-date=2021-02-04|website=Face2Face Africa|language=en}}</ref> He serves as the president of Holospace Laboratories Inc. of [[Camp Hill, Pennsylvania|Camp Hill]], [[Pennsylvania]].

== About ==
Dunkley was born on December 29, 1939, in [[New York (state)|New York]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Kenneth J. Dunkley|url=https://youngstems.com/kenneth-j-dunkley/|url-status=dead|access-date=2021-02-23|website=YoungSTEMs|archive-date=2021-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121232609/https://youngstems.com/kenneth-j-dunkley/}}</ref> Dunkley, who has a master's degree in physics, conducted research in human vision that led to his discovery that a 2-dimensional picture would appear as 3-dimensional if two points in a person's peripheral vision were blocked.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Chubb|first=L. Renee'|date=2019-02-16|title=Black History Month: Unsung Heroes & Their Inventions You Can't Live Without -|url=https://demwritepress.com/2019/02/16/black-history-month-unsung-heroes-their-inventions-you-cant-live-without/|access-date=2021-02-22|website=demwritepress.com|language=en-US}}</ref> This discovery led to future improvements of 3D viewing glasses and the technology we use to view films today.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Phiri|first=Andrew Ose|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zcAeAQAAIAAJ|title=African Scientific Legacy|date=2006|publisher=Mwajionera Enterprises|pages=60|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=African American History Month, Computers in Skirts & More|url=https://benchmarks.it.unt.edu/feb2017-history|access-date=2021-02-23|website=University of North Texas, Information Technology Department}}</ref>

Known as both a visual pioneer and a leader in the field of [[holography]], Dunkley is the president of Holospace Laboratories Inc. and conducts visual effects workshops at the Museum of Scientific Discovery in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania|Harrisburg]], Pennsylvania.<ref name=":1" /> Dunkley also has experience as a [[Microsoft]] and robotics application trainer.<ref name=":0" />
